title: Two-Layer NumPy Network
prompt:
Implement `TwoLayerNet` using only NumPy: two affine layers with ReLU between them and a numerically stable softmax output.

- `__init__(input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim)`: initialize weights and biases.
- `forward(X)`: return class probabilities of shape `(n_samples, output_dim)`.
- `loss(preds, y)`: return mean cross-entropy from normalized class probabilities `preds` of shape `(n_samples, output_dim)` and integer labels `y` of shape `(n_samples,)`. Each `y[i]` is a zero-based class index. Use the supplied probabilities directly without modifying them; do not run `forward` inside `loss`.
- `train_step(X, y, learning_rate=0.1)`: take one gradient descent step and return the updated loss.

Choose your own initialization and internal implementation.

example.reasoning: A softmax classifier returns one normalized probability row per input example.

assets.alt: Two-layer network forward pass, tensor shapes, mean loss, backpropagation and parameter update
assets.caption: 1 / 3 · forward(X) returns P (preds). loss(preds, y) consumes those normalized probabilities and integer labels directly.

assets.caption: 2 / 3 · G = dL/dZ is the combined softmax + cross-entropy gradient with respect to logits. One-hot labels are derivation notation; loss accepts integer y.

assets.caption: 3 / 3 · train_step(X, y) computes all gradients, updates the parameters, then returns loss(forward(X), y) using the updated predictions.
